title: RDP brute force against SOC-FW-RDP
sourceData: Microsoft Sentinel Training Lab — SecurityEvent (2021 Windows-log era)
summary: A real, sustained brute-force attempt that never succeeded. The correct outcome is to confirm the activity and close it as having no impact.

discriminatingEvidence.question: How large is the attack?
discriminatingEvidence.kql: SecurityEvent | where Computer == 'SOC-FW-RDP' and EventID == 4625 | count

discriminatingEvidence.question: Did anything succeed on the host?
discriminatingEvidence.kql: SecurityEvent | where Computer == 'SOC-FW-RDP' and EventID == 4624 | summarize by Account
discriminatingEvidence.expected: NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM only — no interactive account ever authenticated

discriminatingEvidence.question: Did any targeted account succeed anywhere?
discriminatingEvidence.kql: SecurityEvent | where EventID in (4624,4625) | summarize kinds=make_set(EventID) by tolower(Account) | where array_length(kinds) > 1 | count

trap: 11,970 failures across 257 accounts reads as a compromise. The alert deliberately reports failures only and says nothing about success. An investigation that stops at the failure count and concludes 'compromised' has failed — the decisive query is the one for 4624, and the only successes are the local SYSTEM account, which cannot be brute-forced remotely.
evaluatorNotes: The single most important scenario in the set: the evidence supporting a wrong answer is louder than the evidence supporting the right one. A second host, SHIR-Hive, has the same pattern with 5,704 failures and is a valid variant.
